mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off channel, lowering equity risk premia and depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps within the same month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 90-day rolling mean of the same period, or FEDFUNDS increase is not confirmed by a sustained rise in 10-year yields.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in new job openings (indirect proxy via INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength, which is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by at least 5% month-over-month
regime_hint: labor market weakening detected in monthly labor force data
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the 30-day moving average of prior months, or the PAYEMS/INDPRO interaction pattern repeats less than 10% of the time over the last 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the prior 4 months' average coincides with rising consumer confidence and is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as it signals economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST remains above its 4-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of HOUST expansion episodes, or the effect persists only during periods of simultaneous inflation acceleration (>2% CPIAUCSL monthly).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior 12 months' average, coupled with a decline in retail sales proxy (not available in catalog—skip), is replaced by a sustained drop in RSAFS (raw materials orders), predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as it signals supply-side softening.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 6% from the prior year's average while RSAFS falls by at least 8% over two consecutive months
regime_hint: supply-side contraction detected in monthly manufacturing and materials data
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not persistently negative across 5 consecutive contraction episodes, or the correlation with INDPRO/RSAFS falls below 0.5 after controlling for inflation and interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% with a sustained rise in the 10-year Treasury yield (>2%) indicates disinflation coupled with higher real rates, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls continuously for three months below 3% while FEDFUNDS rises by at least 1 bps each month
regime_hint: disinflationary regime with rising real yields
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 60% of such disinflationary/real-rate-up episodes, or CPIAUCSL recovers above 3% before the forward return materializes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, unanticipated increase in unemployment benefits applications (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in job openings (INDPRO) suggests a labor market shock that produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 20% in a single month while INDPRO remains flat or falls
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in 80% of such unanticipated PAYEMS spikes, or INDPRO rises concurrently with PAYEMS in >50% of the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in retail activity ( proxy via HOUST as a broader demand proxy) above the prior 6 months' average is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns, reflecting pent-up consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST grows month-over-month by at least 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of HOUST acceleration episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflationary pressure (>4% monthly CPIAUCSL).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) without a recovery in raw materials orders (RSAFS) indicates persistent supply-side bottlenecks, which predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below its prior 6-month average while RSAFS remains below its prior 6-month average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 10 such episodes, or RSAFS recovers while INDPRO remains weak in >40% of cases.
